Start with project inventory and startup routines, then follow form events into methods and callbacks. Inspect report origins and dry-run branches where present. Ask the original author about business rationale and missing procedures.
How the program starts

The startup block in the Delphi program is where initialization and form creation are normally declared. These are the startup expressions actually captured from the program resource:
No program startup expressions were captured in this scope. Open the DPR source; startup must not be inferred from an arbitrary first routine.
Application.Initialize prepares the application framework; Application.CreateForm declares a form instance; Application.Run enters the event loop when those calls are present. Their presence alone does not establish successful runtime startup.
Follow an event into the code

Start at a serialized event and follow binds to its routine. calls identifies a call site; passes_callback identifies a supplied anonymous routine; schedules is a possible asynchronous connection. Click any object in a trace to continue. None of these facts proves callback timing or runtime order.

Delphi terms explained

Unit: a Pascal module grouping declarations and implementations.
Class/type: a definition of data and available operations. Component: an object declared in a form resource.
Routine: a procedure or function. Signature: the declared parameter and result types. Event handler: a routine connected to an event.
Callback: code supplied for later invocation. Asynchronous: work whose ordering or thread differs from the immediate caller.
Control-flow graph: possible paths through a routine, including branches, loops and exits. Def-use: relationships between writing and reading values.
Static confirmed: supported by a captured declaration or code location. Inferred: a derivation with limits. Unresolved: no supported target was established.
Generation: one captured source/configuration revision. Fingerprint: its hash identity. Detached: historical data open without source attachment.

sections.title: handoff
paragraphs: Project Semantic.dproj; generation 1; Debug / Win32.

Validate artifact hashes, generation and input fingerprints before use. Request authorization before modifying or executing the analyzed project. Treat AI explanations as hypotheses requiring evidence and human review.

Questions for the original author

Ask and record answers against the selected object:
What business result should this operation produce? What inputs are mandatory and what makes them valid?
Which outputs should the user inspect, and what proves success? What can fail and how should a user recover?
Which rule is historical or contractual? What must never change? Which tests cover the behavior?
What must an operator install or configure? Which deployment steps and permissions are required?
For asynchronous paths: which thread owns the operation, how is completion reported, and what cancels it?
Use Knowledge to preserve the named author, evidence and review state. No author answer is generated by a symbol name.
